summary: Our team is developing an astronaut health monitoring software powered by NASA data and realistic simulations. It addresses health safety challenges in outer space by alerting astronauts to critical conditions whenever unsafe signs are detected. This issue is vital because space has always been humanity's ultimate frontier for exploration, requiring brave and resilient individuals to venture beyond Earth. To enable more people to travel into space, ensuring their health remains stable is essential. Therefore, our web application aims to contribute to monitoring and protecting the well-being of these heroes.
details:
Project Overview: ORBITAL is an advanced, sci-fi HUD-themed web dashboard designed for real-time astronaut health tracking and life-support monitoring in space environments.

How it Works & Key Features:The platform provides a futuristic user interface with real-time data visualizers, tracking vital health metrics such as heart rate, blood oxygen levels (SpO2), blood pressure, and telemetry.It includes localized multilingual support and responsive layouts optimized for seamless monitoring across devices.

Benefits & Intended Impact:The project aims to enhance astronaut safety and mission efficiency by offering a clear, instant overview of physiological data during space missions.It helps mission control or crew members proactively manage health risks through intuitive visual alerts and status indicators.

Tools & Technologies Used:Developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and React within a modern component-based structure.Deployed publicly via Netlify for fast, reliable, and accessible cloud hosting.

Creativity & Design Considerations:The team focused heavily on user experience (UX) and immersive sci-fi design elements (HUD layouts, scanlines, and glowing telemetry charts) to bridge futuristic aesthetics with practical utility.Special consideration was given to responsiveness, performance optimization, and multilingual localization to ensure accessibility for an international audience.
dataRefs: Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions
